finding: Low Fill Rates and High Stockout Incidence in Home & Living (South and West)
evidence: The top priority workstream, Home & Living in the South warehouse (covering 20 locations), recorded a fill rate of 75.38%, a stockout rate of 45.0% (9 stockout locations), an at-risk rate of 25.0% (5 at-risk locations), and a potential gross margin exposure of ₹575,632.69 out of 3,257 demand units. Similarly, Home & Living in the West warehouse recorded a fill rate of 79.52%, a stockout rate of 35.0% (7 stockout locations), an at-risk rate of 30.0% (6 at-risk locations), and a potential gross margin exposure of ₹488,275.98 out of 3,310 demand units. Together with Home Appliances in North, the top three workstreams account for 49.61% of the network's total potential gross margin exposure.
hypothesis_unproven: Potential contributors include localized demand surges exceeding safety stock parameters, supplier delivery delays from associated vendors, or lead-time variability. Confirming these hypotheses requires analyzing historical point-of-sale data, vendor PO dispatch logs, and historical safety stock buffer settings.
recommended_action: Execute targeted safety stock buffer reviews and evaluate expedited replenishment schedules from regional suppliers.
illustrative_target: Raise category fill rate to 88.0% (an improvement of 12.62 percentage points for South and 8.48 percentage points for West).
verification_method: Weekly inventory position audits and stockout incident logging.

finding: Critical Zero-Stock SKU Locations Associated with Margin Exposure
evidence: Multiple high-volume SKUs registered zero closing stock while facing heavy unfulfilled demand. Specifically, SKU0051 (Home & Living Product 11) in the South warehouse (supplied by SUP005) had 0 closing stock units, a reorder point of 119 units, 198 unfulfilled units, and a calculated margin exposure of ₹303,759.72. The same SKU in the West warehouse had 0 closing stock units, a reorder point of 110 units, 190 unfulfilled units, and a calculated margin exposure of ₹291,486.60. Furthermore, SKU0043 in North (SUP005) had 0 closing stock units, 170 unfulfilled units, and ₹155,298.40 exposure; SKU0109 in West (SUP011) had 0 closing stock units, 92 unfulfilled units, and ₹152,360.28 exposure; and SKU0111 in North (SUP011) had 0 closing stock units, 72 unfulfilled units, and ₹151,948.80 exposure.
hypothesis_unproven: Hypotheses include supplier manufacturing bottlenecks, delayed purchase order placements, or sudden demand spikes exceeding lead-time coverage. Confirming these requires reviewing enterprise resource planning (ERP) purchase order generation logs and supplier production capacity reports.
recommended_action: Implement emergency vendor expediting and establish automated replenishment triggers for critical zero-stock SKUs.
illustrative_target: Restore positive closing inventory at all five flagged SKU–warehouse locations (four distinct SKUs), while measuring stockout-day incidents separately. Positive closing stock does not retroactively eliminate earlier stockout days.

evidence: Several suppliers exhibit low on-time delivery rates; these may increase planning risk, but the available data do not demonstrate that their delays caused unfulfilled demand. SUP007 (Nexa Vendor 07) recorded an on-time rate of 75.81% across 62 eligible deliveries (47 on-time) with a weighted lead time of 13.37 days and ₹37,506.18 in potential gross margin exposure. SUP001 (Nexa Vendor 01) recorded an on-time rate of 79.03% across 62 eligible deliveries (49 on-time), a weighted lead time of 12.95 days, and ₹130,180.84 in exposure. SUP003 (Nexa Vendor 03) recorded an on-time rate of 80.00% across 55 eligible deliveries (44 on-time), a weighted lead time of 5.64 days, and ₹106,164.38 in exposure. Additionally, SUP005 (Nexa Vendor 05), while achieving an 87.72% on-time rate, is associated with a massive ₹952,652.45 in potential gross margin exposure associated with its supplied SKUs; its delivery scorecard includes 57 eligible deliveries and a 13.89-day weighted lead time.
hypothesis_unproven: Hypotheses include carrier capacity constraints, raw material shortages at vendor facilities, or inaccurate lead-time planning assumptions. Confirming these requires supplier audit reports and transportation transit log analyses.
recommended_action: Conduct supplier performance reviews with SUP007, SUP001, and SUP003, and evaluate contractual remediation (conditional on contractual review).
illustrative_target: Improve supplier on-time delivery rates for SUP007, SUP001, and SUP003 to a minimum of 90.00% (improvements of 14.19, 10.97, and 10.00 percentage points, respectively).

finding: High Overall Network Stockout and At-Risk Incidence
evidence: Across the network of 360 locations, 79 locations (21.94%) experienced stockouts during October 2026, and 141 locations (39.17%) were categorized as at-risk (closing stock positive and below reorder point). This reflects an increase in stockout rate compared to September 2026 (18.89% or 68 locations) and a slight increase in at-risk rate from September (37.22% or 134 locations), even as the total network fill rate improved slightly from 92.09% to 92.87%.
hypothesis_unproven: Potential root causes include static reorder point parameters that fail to account for demand volatility, or safety stock allocations that are misaligned with regional demand profiles. Confirming these requires a network-wide inventory policy simulation.
recommended_action: Recalibrate reorder points and safety stock thresholds dynamically across all 360 locations.
illustrative_target: Reduce stockout rate to 12.00% (an improvement of 9.94 percentage points) and at-risk rate to 25.00% (an improvement of 14.17 percentage points).

finding: Above-Network Lead Times Among Selected Suppliers
evidence: The network weighted lead time stood at 10.86 days across 729 eligible lead-time deliveries (7,920.0 weighted lead days). Several suppliers have observed lead times above the network average, which warrants replenishment-risk review but does not establish that lead times caused individual stockouts; for example, SUP005 has a weighted lead time of 13.89 days, SUP009 has 13.43 days, SUP007 has 13.37 days, and SUP008 has 12.97 days.
hypothesis_unproven: Hypotheses include carrier transit variability, purchase-order processing delays, or supplier production scheduling. Confirming these requires logistics transit time breakdowns and vendor operational workflow audits.
recommended_action: Negotiate lead-time service level agreements (SLAs) and optimize inbound logistics routing for high-delay suppliers (conditional on contractual review).
illustrative_target: Reduce network weighted lead time from 10.86 days to 9.00 days (a reduction of 1.86 days).
verification_method: Inbound shipment tracking and GRN (Goods Receipt Note) timestamp audits.
